SMTO-LLM-0034 — Model response did not match the expected schema

GUID: ca00295a-d479-4cf8-8018-11d992183b54
Slug: llm-schema-validation-error
Domain: LLM · Subsystem: provider

What happened

  • The model's answer was readable, but some details were wrong, such as a missing part, the wrong kind of value or a repeated entry. SMTO didn't use it, because it could make the next step go wrong.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Settings › Setup › Model routing, open the Main card, and select Check saved model. It tests whether this model can fill in a simple required form correctly.
  2. If the check passes, try the work once more in a new task. If the same message comes back, stop retrying and go to the next step. An occasional slip may not repeat, but the same mistake twice means the model can't handle this request.
  3. Pick a more capable model in the Main card, or ask the person who runs your model service to turn on strict format support. Select Save Main and start a new task. Smaller models and servers without format enforcement more often leave out or mistype details.

What success looks like

  • The task's next step completes and moves on without this message.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO or your model service. Don't keep repeating the same request unchanged; it tends to fail the same way.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A decoded structured result or tool-argument object failed validation against the requested schema (missing required field, wrong type or value, duplicate key, or a non-JSON number such as NaN).

What this means

  • A decoded result or argument violates the required shape, type or value constraints; duplicate keys and non-JSON numbers can also be rejected at the argument boundary. This category concerns model preparation or response acceptance. It does not reverse earlier operations or establish their outcome; their receipts remain authoritative.

Why this can happen

  • A decoded result or argument violates the required shape, type or value constraints; duplicate keys and non-JSON numbers can also be rejected at the argument boundary.

How to diagnose it

  • Use the bounded validation path to distinguish missing fields, wrong types, duplicate keys and prohibited numeric values; compare it with the advertised schema.

How to fix it

  • Read the validation errors and schema name in the error details to find the failing field. Confirm the serving stack enforces the tool or JSON schema for this model (guided decoding or a matching tool-call parser); if the model still produces non-conforming output, use a more capable model for this role in Settings › Setup › Model routing. Do not relax the schema to accept the bad value.
  • Inspect the safe validation path and provider structured-output support.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • The complete value passes the same schema and argument checks before it is consumed.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • This category concerns model preparation or response acceptance. It does not reverse earlier operations or establish their outcome; their receipts remain authoritative.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
